transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Hello, thank you for seeing me. I'm a bit embarrassed to be here, but I keep trying to get rid of what I eat after I overdo it, and I feel like I can’t stop doing it on my own.
To help me understand your situation better, could you tell me your current height and weight, and if you have recently lost a significant amount of weight?

Honestly, I don't know my exact weight offhand because I try to avoid the scale as much as possible due to anxiety about my size. My primary doctor did want me to lose weight for my health, but I don't think I have actually lost a significant amount.
Even if you don't know the exact number, would you say your current weight is considered underweight, normal weight, or overweight for your height?

According to my primary doctor's comments about my BMI, I am considered overweight. He has been really pushing for weight loss to help with my blood pressure and joint pain, which has made me so self-conscious about my size. I just feel like a failure who can't stop myself from getting bigger.
How often do these episodes of overeating and trying to get rid of the food happen, and for how many months have you been experiencing this?

This has been going on for about seven months, ever since my husband's health worsened and my doctor started pushing me about my weight. It happens at least once or twice a week, usually on the stressful days when I am exhausted from caregiving.
Do you have a specific target weight that you feel you absolutely must achieve, and is this target weight significantly below what would be considered a healthy weight for you?

I don't really have a specific target weight in mind, and I'm certainly not trying to become underweight. I'm just incredibly distressed by how big I feel and failing my doctor's expectations about my BMI, and I just want to stop myself from getting any bigger.
When you have these episodes of overeating, do you feel a complete loss of control over your eating, and what methods do you use to try to 'get rid of' the food?

Yes, it's like a switch flips and I go into a trance, unable to stop my hands from reaching for more food even when I'm uncomfortably full. Afterward, out of sheer panic, I go into the bathroom, turn on the fan so my husband won't hear, and make myself throw up to try and erase what I've done.
Besides making yourself throw up, do you ever use other methods to prevent weight gain, such as taking laxatives, diet pills, or fasting for long periods?
No, I have never used laxatives, diet pills, or tried to fast. Making myself throw up is the only thing I've resorted to, even though I feel deeply ashamed of it every single time.
How much do your weight and body shape influence how you judge your self-worth as a person? Does it completely dominate how you feel about yourself?

Yes, it completely dominates how I feel about myself, and I feel so ashamed of it. Ever since my doctor brought up my BMI, I can't look in a mirror without focusing on my stomach and arms and thinking I'm a complete failure. No matter what good things I do for my husband or my church, these negative thoughts about my body completely take over my self-worth.

You mentioned this happens at least once or twice a week. Over the last three months, has this consistently occurred at least twice every single week, or are there some weeks where it only happens once?

It definitely varies depending on how stressful things are with my husband's care, so there are some weeks where it only happens once. However, it has consistently happened at least once or twice every single week for the past several months.
During these episodes of overeating, can you describe the amount of food you typically consume? Would you say it is a much larger amount of food than most people would eat in a similar short period?

Yes, it is definitely a much larger amount than normal. On stressful nights when I'm alone in the kitchen, I'll eat half a pan of brownies, several dinner rolls with butter, and whatever leftovers are in the fridge in one sitting. Once I start, it's like a switch flips and I just can't stop myself.
On average, over the past three months, would you say these episodes of overeating followed by throwing up occurred at least twice a week, or has the average been less than that?

On average, yes, it has been happening about once or twice a week over the last three months. It usually aligns with the particularly difficult days of caring for my husband when I'm just completely worn out. It's a terrible, stressful cycle, and I feel so much shame that I can't seem to stop it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits episodes of binge eating (consuming large quantities of food with a loss of control) followed by compensatory purging (self-induced vomiting) occurring once or twice a week for seven months. While she experiences significant distress and her self-worth is heavily influenced by her body shape and weight, she does not set a weight threshold well below healthy weight and is currently overweight, wishing only to stop gaining weight rather than trying to become underweight. Because she lacks this key feature of bulimia nervosa (F50.2) and is of excessive weight, she meets the criteria for atypical bulimia nervosa (F50.3).
